response.sql: SELECT l.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) as avg_ALP, AVG(l.HCT) as avg_HCT FROM Laboratory l INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.`U-PRO` = '-' AND l.RA = '-' GROUP BY l.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY CASE WHEN avg_HCT IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, avg_HCT DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The clause 'For patients who have tested '-' for both' filters the Laboratory records to only those where BOTH U-PRO = '-' AND RA = '-', and averages are calculated from those filtered records. An alternative reading would identify the patient pool by this criterion but average across ALL their laboratory records.

The phrase 'ignoring missing values' means NULL values in ALP and HCT columns are excluded from averages (standard SQL AVG behavior). Rounding is not applied by SQL; the output format controls display precision.

alternatives.interpretation: Identify patients who have at least one laboratory record where both U-PRO = '-' AND RA = '-', then calculate ALP and HCT averages across ALL their laboratory records (not just those matching both conditions).
alternatives.sql: SELECT l.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) as avg_ALP, AVG(l.HCT) as avg_HCT FROM Laboratory l INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.ID IN (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-') GROUP BY l.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY CASE WHEN avg_HCT IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, avg_HCT DESC LIMIT 10
